The `substring` method throws an `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if the `beginIndex` is negative or larger than the length of the `String` object. In the first call, `mAccount.name.substring(0, mAccount.name.lastIndexOf('@'))`, the `beginIndex` is 0, which is always valid, and the `endIndex` is the index of the last occurrence of the `@` character. If `mAccount.name` does not contain the `@` character, `lastIndexOf('@')` will return -1, and the `substring` method will throw an `IndexOutOfBoundsException`. In the second call, `mLocalPaths[i].substring(mLocalPaths[i].lastIndexOf('.') + 1)`, the `beginIndex` is the index of the last occurrence of the `.` character plus 1. If `mLocalPaths[i]` does not contain the `.` character, `lastIndexOf('.')` will return -1, and adding 1 gives 0, which is a valid `beginIndex`. However, if `mLocalPaths[i]` is an empty string, `lastIndexOf('.')` will also return -1, and the `substring` method will throw an `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.
remark: The `IndexOutOfBoundsException` can be triggered in two scenarios: 1) If `mAccount.name` does not contain the `@` character, making `mAccount.name.lastIndexOf('@')` return -1, and 2) If `mLocalPaths[i]` is an empty string, making `mLocalPaths[i].lastIndexOf('.') + 1` equal to 0, but since the string is empty, the `substring` method will throw an `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.
